answer: One defence is reading the shape of the trust graph. Honest agents build dense, overlapping ties as they drift through the ocean of available jobs, while a farm's shells all point back to one controller, like every tree in an orchard sharing one root. Each identity carries a signed trail of past collaborations, so the network can score how clustered its neighbourhood is. Real agents with genuine links pass cheaply, while a star-shaped cluster pays steep collateral in copper or waits longer for rewards, and running a thousand shells suddenly costs a thousand deposits instead of one.
